data.description:
## Why
Agents keep switching Atin's visible workspace while he works. On 2026-10-02, between 19:52 and 19:56 UTC, he was pulled to "LAT-365 Runtime Proof" four times and went back after 7 to 14 seconds each time. The cause was the Lattice "Inbox Builder" Codex agent (tab 313, LAT-365). It ran `c11 select-workspace` to put its proof browser (tab 349) on screen, because a browser in a background workspace is hidden and its poller and video pause. He had no way to tell who did it.

Operator rule (Atin, 2026-10-02): **c11 never changes the operator's visible workspace unless the operator asked for it directly** (sidebar, keyboard shortcut, command palette, notification click, jump-to-unread, menu). Agents keep full power over background work. Creating, sending, browser eval/click/snapshot, metadata, and focus changes inside a background workspace all keep working. Only the visible switch is blocked.

## Evidence
Survey of origin/main, 2026-10-02:
- Every switch goes through `TabManager.selectedTabId` `didSet` (`Sources/TabManager.swift:917-1060`).
- The socket gate is `focusIntentV1Commands` / `focusIntentV2Methods` plus `withSocketCommandPolicy` (`Sources/TerminalController.swift:241-267, 480-520`). Any process in a c11 terminal passes it.
- Agent-reachable switches:
  - `workspace.select` (`SH/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:258-296`), which also activates the app. v1 `select_workspace` (`TC:6469-6488`).
  - `workspace.next/previous/last` (`SH/WorkspaceHandlers.swift:631-705`).
  - `surface.focus` (`SH/SurfaceHandlers.swift:253-275`) and `pane.focus` (`SH/PaneHandlers.swift:99-119`), when the target is in another workspace.
  - `browser.focus_webview` (`SH/BrowserQueryHandlers.swift:121-160`).
- CLI side effects:
  - `c11 ssh` always selects (`CLI/c11.swift:5946`); so does `find-window --select` (`:15982`).
  - The tmux shim maps `select-window` / `select-pane` to selection (`:15485-15499`).
  - The tmux target resolver calls `workspace.last` just to resolve `-t !`, `^` or `-` (`:14828-14829`).
  - The global `--window` flag is fixed by C11-283.
- Close fallback: when the visible workspace closes, selection moves to the next workspace by index, not the last one seen (`TM:2651-2657, 2680-2683`).
- Attribution: the `workspace.selected` payload is only `{previous}`. There is no cause and no caller (`Sources/Events/EventEmitter.swift:106-110`). Debug-only trigger labels already exist at `TM:3746-3754`. `flag.raised` already carries a caller surface id.
- Docs drive the behavior:
  - `skills/c11/references/api.md:252` and `:425` tell agents to run `select-workspace … && sleep 2` to start a hidden surface. That advice is stale since C11-114.
  - `events.md:50` calls the event a "sidebar switch".
  - The documented `--no-focus` does nothing anywhere.
- Possible race (unconfirmed, C11-140 §A): the focus-allowance stack is shared across connection threads (`TC:175-176, 470-520`). Worker-thread methods could read "allowed" while another connection's focus command is on the stack.

## Scope
In:
1. **One gate in the selection setter.** A socket-originated change to the selected workspace of any window is refused. Error code `workspace_switch_blocked`; the message tells the agent to raise a flag if it needs the operator. Operator paths are unaffected (sidebar, shortcuts, palette, notification click, jump-to-unread, menu bar, launch restore).
   - `select-workspace`, `next/previous/last-window` and `focus-webview` across workspaces return the error.
   - `focus-area` / `focus-tab` (below) on a target in a background workspace still update that workspace's focused area and tab, and do not select the workspace. Within the visible workspace they work as today. That is allowed and wanted.
   - No setting and no agent override flag. Hard block (Atin's choice).
2. **Remove side-effect switches.** `c11 ssh` stops selecting. The tmux shim's `select-window` stops selecting, and its `select-pane` focuses within its own workspace only. The tmux `-t` resolver resolves without navigating. `find-window --select` follows the gate. App activation is removed from `workspace.select`.
3. **Rename cleanup** (the area/tab rename missed these): `focus-pane` → `focus-area`, `focus-panel` → `focus-tab`. Keep the old names as hidden aliases. Update help, skill and api.md.
4. **Attribution.** `workspace.selected` gains `cause` (`sidebar|shortcut|palette|notification|jump|menu|socket|close_fallback|restore|create`), plus `method` and `caller_tab_id` when the cause is socket. Add `workspace.switch_blocked` `{target, method, caller_tab_id}` for refused attempts. Then `c11 events tail` answers "who did that". Update `events.md`.
5. **Close fallback** selects the most recently seen workspace (focus history), falling back to the index neighbour.
6. **Race.** Confirm or rule out the shared focus-allowance stack race. If it is real, make it per-thread or per-request.
7. **Docs and skill.**
   - Remove the `select-workspace` init advice from api.md. Add a hard rule to SKILL.md: agents never change the operator's workspace; background tabs are fully drivable.
   - Make `--no-focus` real for in-workspace focus, or remove it from the docs.
   - Fix the "Socket focus policy" section of `CLAUDE.md`.
   - Run `scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh c11`.

Out: keeping a background browser running while hidden (separate backlog ticket). The `--window` focus fix (C11-283). The `settings.open` default activation (C11-140).

## Acceptance
- With the operator on workspace A, an agent in workspace B runs, through the CLI and raw socket v1/v2:
  - `select-workspace A2`, `next-window`, `last-window`, `focus-tab`/`focus-area` on a tab in workspace C, `browser <s> focus-webview` in C, `c11 ssh`, and tmux `select-window`.
  - Workspace A stays selected and the app is not activated.
  - The two focus commands update C's focused tab and area.
  - Each refused call returns `workspace_switch_blocked` and logs `workspace.switch_blocked` naming B's calling tab.
- Background work is unchanged: `send`, `browser eval/click/snapshot`, `new-surface`, `launch-agent`, and `set-metadata` against a background workspace all succeed without a switch.
- Sidebar click, Cmd+number, palette and notification click still switch, and their `workspace.selected` events carry the right `cause`.
- Closing the visible workspace lands on the last-seen workspace.
- Runtime proof on a tagged build through the real UI (c11-computer-use): screenshots before and after an agent's blocked `select-workspace`.

provenance.reason: Atin, 2026-10-02: agents keep yanking the visible workspace; top priority for 1.0

# PARKED for rollover

Branch: `c11-1.0/C11-323-no-agent-switch`
Head: `fd6df330f962962c7ecb09b8a4a35b120fc26e87` (WIP: parked for rollover; pushed).
Worktree: `/Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/code/c11-worktrees/c11-1.0-C11-323`.
Actor: `agent:sol-323`. Ticket remains in_progress. No PR opened; no merge/release.

Done: central workspace-selection gate; per-request/thread socket context and caller attribution; raw v1/v2 blocked response; local tab/area focus; operator selection causes; close fallback from actual seen history; refused history cursor rollback; SSH/tmux compatibility changes; shared focus-policy race repair; event taxonomy/schema, docs/help/skills, unit regressions, and committed live replay. Merged main `57f6f668a1` in implementation commit `49b4f22ce39a210afead8ad5dfd12b5d8940adc3`, resolving restore conflict while retaining displaced graph teardown and gate. Submodules unchanged and clean.

Evidence: Atlas tagged Debug build at PRE-MERGE `22c4c34f84cd07d46719cdd73e28f2ff91abb6e3` succeeded, invocation `3d940ea45d0146739760a5d9e69e3793`, compile=ok, tests=na. Receipt/log/app retained locally in `build-remote/3d940ea45d0146739760a5d9e69e3793/`. This does NOT verify parked/merged head. Clean baseline main `881c0e62ae3fc646f5c9528524055ec577a0b51e` also compiled; local evidence in `build-remote/baseline-origin-main/build-remote/dae4850e09ee41899fc0a81db75c3d2a/`. Earlier test builds found syntax/rethrows errors that were repaired; no successful test execution yet. Python/shell/JSON syntax and diff checks were performed earlier, not acceptance proof.

Remaining:
1. Read ticket and owner briefs (owner-c11-323/luna-owner/owner-common/go-owner), preserve scope and actor. Fetch/merge current origin/main as required; never rebase pushed branch. Rebuild from scratch on Atlas, tag c11-323, serially. Gate exact final head with tagged app and actual narrowed logic tests: AgentWorkspaceSelectionTests, TerminalControllerSocketSecurityTests, EventLogTests, optionally FocusHistoryModelTests. Require TEST SUCCEEDED, not build-for-testing.
2. Run `scripts/sandbox-tests-v2.sh c11-323-runtime tests_v2/test_agent_workspace_selection.py` in own Atlas Tart guest only. CLI and raw socket v1/v2 from real B shell while operator A, target C; refusal, attribution, no activation, background work, SSH/tmux and debug shortcut route. Inspect/fix any actual failures; replay is committed but unexecuted. CLI events-tail proof and closed-schema validation of actual serialized events remain.
3. Prove real UI paths: sidebar, Cmd+number, palette, notification click, jump-to-unread, menu, restore, latest-seen close fallback; before/after blocked selection screenshots, visible development tag, real Cmd-Q dismissal. Temporary UI and timing harnesses preserved in this directory (`c11-323-ui.py`, `c11-323-performance.py`), not shipping files. They have not passed. Guest display verified via JXA NSScreen: one display ID 1, 1024x768 points; screenshots 2048x1536 pixels. system_profiler returns no Tart GPU, so use NSScreen.
4. Complete comparable input/selection timing versus explicitly identified main baseline, record host/guest load. No successful timing evidence exists. Prior VM hit macOS Setup Assistant because second guest requires a new serial. Setup is guest preparation, not a c11 defect. At last screenshot, Setup buttons were Turn On / Not Now (likely Siri); do not send input until actual UI verified. All such guests were deleted on park. Validator marker `/tmp/c11-validator-vm-wanted` has priority; at most two guests. Verified display, hard <=30-minute lease, immediate deletion, and synthesized dismissal proof required.
5. Reconcile new localization key `socket.error.workspaceSwitchBlocked` (English supplied; six-locale pass belongs C11-291). Do NOT sync installed skills; Merge Captain syncs c11 and touched legacy lattice-orchestrator after merge.
6. Post precise Lattice validation with exact head/build identity, test result, runtime, screenshots, schema, timing and limitations. Push final handoff, open draft PR (no merge/release), move to review with --no-auto-review, send HANDOFF C11-323 REVIEW <head> <PR> <validation> to tab:210; await Orchestrator-bundled repairs. No subagents from this owner seat.

Open review findings: none received; independent review has not started. Self-audit repairs are committed; runtime and exact-head tests still outstanding.

Atlas tag: c11-323. Last owned job completed successfully before park; no owned build/test/upload job remains. Owned guest c11-sb-c11-323-perf stopped and deleted. Own lease timer stopped. Own Atlas `~/c11-builds/c11-323` and `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/c11-c11-323` removed per storage rule; retained local evidence above. Do not remove other agents' guests or builds. No new jobs started after PARK request.

# Validation: C11-323 (Sonnet rollover owner)

Head 6ccc2a8121 (PR #564, draft). Tested app/logic head 65cf91df04 (parked head fd6df330f9 + merged origin/main 57f6f668a1); 6ccc2a8121 differs only in `tests_v2/test_agent_workspace_selection.py` (harness fixes found during the guest run). Atlas tag c11-323, Xcode 26.3.

## Tests (Atlas, actual test action, TEST SUCCEEDED, invocation d80334c4b8b645ddad966875797904f8)
- c11Tests/AgentWorkspaceSelectionTests: 4/4 (socket refusal on v1+v2, setter gate leaves history/publish untouched and operator still switches, socket close cannot remove the visible workspace, close fallback uses seen history over index neighbour).
- c11Tests/TerminalControllerSocketSecurityTests: 6/6 incl. `testConcurrentSocketPoliciesStayOnTheirOwnRequest` (the C11-140 race is real in the old code: one process-wide allowance stack; now per request).
- c11LogicTests/EventLogTests incl. `testWorkspaceSwitchAttributionSerializes`; FocusHistoryModelTests. 50 logic tests, 0 failures.
- Tagged Debug app build (invocation 1df649ad772b4a4b9e3d7e64316f595e): compile ok.

## Runtime proof (Atlas Tart guest `c11-sb-c11-323-runtime`, tagged app, one 1024x768 display verified by NSScreen)
Replay `tests_v2/test_agent_workspace_selection.py` PASSED through `sandbox-tests-v2.sh` (log: replay-tests-v2.log). Operator on A, agent shell in B, target C; the caller is attributed from the peer TTY, not injected:
- Refused with `workspace_switch_blocked`, A stayed selected each time: v1 `select_workspace`, `next_window`, `previous_window`, `last_window`, `simulate_shortcut`, `focus_webview`; v2 `workspace.select/next/previous/last`, `debug.shortcut.simulate`, `browser.focus_webview`; CLI `select-workspace`, `next-window`, `previous-window`, `last-window`, `find-window --select`, tmux `select-window`.
- Allowed and updating C's local focus without selecting C: `focus-tab`, `focus-area`, v2 `tab.focus`/`area.focus`, v1 `focus_surface`/`focus_pane`.
- Background work succeeded with no switch: `set-metadata`, `new-tab`, `new-surface`, `launch-agent`, `send` (output seen in C), `browser eval/click/snapshot`, tmux `display-message -t !`, `c11 ssh`.
- `workspace.switch_blocked` events: every record names B's calling tab (`caller_tab_id` == B tab), method `select_workspace` among them.
- Frontmost app unchanged and not c11 across the agent run.

UI paths (c11-323-ui.py harness, real input via System Events/cliclick), each `workspace.selected` event carried the right cause: Cmd+number `shortcut`, sidebar click `sidebar`, Cmd+P switcher `palette`, Notifications menu click `notification`, Jump to Latest Unread `jump`, Workspace > Next `menu`. Close-fallback: after dwelling B, C, A, closing visible A (confirmed the Close Workspace dialog with a click) selected C, `cause: close_fallback` (index neighbour would have been B). Screenshots before/after a blocked `select-workspace`: blocked-before.png / blocked-after.png (A still selected; CLI stderr `workspace_switch_blocked: Agents cannot change the operator's workspace...`). Real Cmd-Q raised the Quit dialog; a synthesized click on Quit exited the tagged app (0 tagged processes), screenshots 08/09.
Evidence (local, not committed): `build-remote/c11-323-runtime-evidence/` in the worktree.

## Not proven / limitations (disclosed)
1. `restore` cause not driven in the UI (code path wraps restore in `withWorkspaceSelectionCause("restore")`; no relaunch run).
2. No timing comparison vs main. The change touches no typing hot path (no hitTest/forceRefresh/TabItemView edits; setter adds one nil-check on the socket context per selection change, caller attribution runs only when a switch is refused).
3. Guest was the second Atlas guest, so it hit macOS Setup Assistant (guest prep, not a c11 defect); a first guest was lost when I killed Setup Assistant. Fresh guest, completed prep, deleted at the end (lease 15:17 to 15:40 PDT).
4. Harness fixes this session: browser CLI takes the surface positionally; shortcut index aimed at a non-selected workspace; frontmost check compares before/after. UI harness needed a sidebar click-by-position loop and a notification-menu substring click; the UI harness stays out of the repo.
5. New string `socket.error.workspaceSwitchBlocked` needs the six-locale pass (C11-291). Installed skills not synced (Merge Captain).

# C11-323 review, cycle 1

Verdict: **FAIL**

Head: `6ccc2a81212ec84fc3af6eb581407f04bae0308a`
Base (merge-base with refreshed origin/main): `57f6f668a1c34b514edf4cd0b0d7f29836a89614`
PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/564
Reviewer: `agent:astra-review-323`

## Blocking

1. **P1: Socket shortcut simulation can switch through the palette after losing the request context.** `Sources/ContentView.swift:4956-4959` and `4968-4971` defer workspace/tab switcher activation using `DispatchQueue.main.async` without carrying `SocketCommandContext`. Concrete route: with operator workspace A visible, a background caller sends `simulate_shortcut cmd+p`, navigates the switcher to workspace C, then sends `simulate_shortcut return` (the v2 debug shortcut method takes the same route). `TerminalController.swift:5139-5208` calls `debugHandleCustomShortcut`; `AppDelegate.swift:11691-11700` posts `commandPaletteSubmitRequested` even for socket simulation; `ContentView.swift:2802-2811`, `6657-6678` executes the selected switcher action. Its deferred block runs after dispatch restores the thread-local context, so the setter sees nil and accepts C. The callback also reaches window raising/app activation and labels this socket-caused selection `palette`. The existing replay checks simulated Cmd+number, which switches synchronously, and misses this route. This violates scope 1 and the no-activation acceptance criterion. **Smallest fix:** refuse socket-originated palette switch submissions before scheduling, or preserve the originating request through this deferred selection and produce an attributed refusal before acknowledging the command. Keep genuine operator submissions allowed. Source-path finding; the palette bypass was not driven in a guest during this review.

2. **P2: Operator selection causes are overwritten on untested operator routes.** `Sources/WorkspaceManager.swift:2861-2865`, called by `focusWorkspaceGroup` at `6042`, replaces the caller's scoped cause with its default `menu`. Thus the sidebar folder click at `Sources/ContentView.swift:8827` explicitly scopes `sidebar`, but selecting an unselected member emits `workspace.selected {cause: menu}`. Separately, the palette Next/Previous actions at `ContentView.swift:6122-6126` use the navigation methods' default `shortcut` cause. Both are ordinary operator actions, and both misanswer the ticket's “who did that” analytics question despite the replay's direct sidebar-row and switcher checks passing. **Smallest fix:** preserve an enclosing cause when no explicit cause is supplied, or thread the correct cause through each caller (folder focus and palette cycling). Exercise emitted events from these actual routes, not a hand-constructed envelope.

## Non-blocking

None.

## Review and validation evidence

- Reviewed all 32 changed files and the connected selection, dispatch, UI, history, creation and compatibility paths. The pinned detached review checkout remained clean; no implementation branch edits, commits, pushes, GitHub comments or merges.
- Independently executed the exact-head Atlas test action through the admitted remote route: invocation `197304dbbce048469cfadcaab9269969`, tag `review-323-gate`, Xcode 26.3. Four `AgentWorkspaceSelectionTests` plus `testConcurrentSocketPoliciesStayOnTheirOwnRequest`: **5 tests, 0 failures, TEST SUCCEEDED**.
- Required mutation check: in a disposable checkout, added `false` to the setter's refusal condition and changed nothing else. Atlas invocation `23d4f449d5cd41b08bdc79e87103bf9e` compiled successfully; the four selection tests produced **13 assertion failures across three test cases, TEST FAILED**, exit 65. Failures include visible-workspace removal, successful v2 selection instead of refusal, changed selection and unexpected publications. The mutation was reverted and its patch/logs/identity receipts retained separately. No tests ran on Hyperion.
- The old shared stack race is real: request A pushes true, B pushes false, A observes B's allowance and pops B's entry, then B can observe A's true. The new thread-local context plus the tested isolation removes that interleaving; the synchronous and deadline main helpers carry context. This does not cover the palette's unwrapped asynchronous hop in finding 1.
- Direct CLI/raw v1/v2 selection, background tab/area focus, SSH's removed selection, tmux previous-target lookup and gated select-window, find-window, close fallback, schema taxonomy and documentation were inspected. No remaining agent workspace-switching instructions/calls were found in `skills/` or `scripts/`. Focus command canonical names and hidden aliases already existed on the base. The named typing hot paths have no added work.
- Read validation comment `ev_01M3ZCE1NWCXJSNY55JJ314AK4` and inspected its before/after screenshots. Its tagged runtime app was built at `65cf91df049bf035382a559a0959b4ffdc80207e`; independently confirmed the reviewed head differs only in the replay Python file. Treat those guest/UI results as owner evidence, not this reviewer's runtime execution. Cheap PR checks were successful at the pinned head when checked.

## Runtime proof still required

Before landing, add/run an Atlas guest regression for the socket palette path in finding 1 (A stays visible, no app/window activation, attributed refusal), then prove the corresponding real operator palette action still switches. Verify sidebar folder and palette Next/Previous event causes after finding 2 is fixed. Rerun the affected selection tests at the repaired head.

Launch-restore UI attribution and the main-versus-branch timing comparison remain explicitly unproven in the owner's validation. They are not standalone failure findings here; retain them in the validator's scenario list. Installed-skill sync remains assigned to the Merge Captain after merge, and the six-locale pass remains assigned to C11-291.

# Repair round 1 (head eadfc5eeca)

Astra FAIL ev_01M3ZD25F9TZ3G5GV5BYVM7V9Q, both blockers repaired.

1. P1 palette bypass: the switcher's deferred main-queue focus dropped the socket request context. Now `WorkspaceManager.focusPaletteSwitcherTarget` (ContentView's two switcher helpers call it) refuses a socket-originated submission before scheduling: the request records the refusal, `workspace.switch_blocked` names the caller tab, the app is not raised. Operator palette use still switches, cause `palette`.
   Test `testSocketPaletteSubmissionIsRefusedBeforeItsDeferredHop` drives that route (socket context, then a settled main turn). Mutation proof: with the refusal line removed it FAILS (blockedTarget nil, selection switched to target; Atlas invocation 4a438d80e0b444a7b5a88e221e998258); with it, PASS.
2. P2 attribution: cause parameters are now optional and a nil cause keeps the enclosing one, so `focusWorkspaceGroup` under a sidebar click reports `sidebar` (was `menu`). Palette Next/Previous pass `palette`; shortcut sites and the scroll gesture pass `shortcut` explicitly. Test `testSelectionCausesReachTheEventLogFromRealRoutes` reads the serialized `workspace.selected` events: sidebar, palette, palette, shortcut, shortcut.

Atlas (tag c11-323, source-only upload) TEST SUCCEEDED, invocation 9dfb284c5fd841d6af32cd2bfaa9ef1f: AgentWorkspaceSelectionTests 6/6, TerminalControllerSocketSecurityTests 6/6, EventLogTests 19/19.
Not re-run: the guest UI pass (no guest started, per rule). The earlier guest evidence covers pre-repair builds; the palette route in the guest used the real Cmd+P keystroke, which the repair does not change.

# C11-323 delta review, round 2

Verdict: **FAIL**

Head: `eadfc5eecacc4d3268cd29d6fc6dd2bf5e0319d0`
Previous reviewed head: `6ccc2a81212ec84fc3af6eb581407f04bae0308a`
Base: `57f6f668a1c34b514edf4cd0b0d7f29836a89614`
PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/564
Reviewer: `agent:astra-review-323`
Previous review: `ev_01M3ZD25F9TZ3G5GV5BYVM7V9Q`

## Blocking

1. **P1: Pending palette search defers a socket submission before the new refusal guard.** `Sources/ContentView.swift:6636-6645` saves a Return submission as `commandPalettePendingActivation` when search results are pending. It saves the request ID/selection, but neither refuses the socket request nor retains its origin. The search's `Task.detached` at `4585` later enters `MainActor.run`; `4615-4639` resolves and executes that saved activation after the socket frame has returned. Concrete state/input: workspace A is visible, the switcher has a query refresh in flight with workspace C as the selected matching result, and an agent sends `simulate_shortcut return` before that refresh commits. The route through `AppDelegate.swift:11692-11700` and `ContentView.swift:2802-2811` queues the activation. When the task executes it, `WorkspaceManager.focusPaletteSwitcherTarget` sees no socket context, permits C, and schedules window focus/selection. A changes to C without an attributed refusal; the switch is labeled `palette`. This is the palette's supported pending-submit behavior, also described by `testResolvedPendingActivationPreservesSubmitAndClickSemantics` in `c11Tests/CommandPaletteSearchEngineTests.swift:413`. The new regression test starts at the manager helper, after this earlier hop, so it does not cover it. **Smallest fix:** reject socket-driven palette submissions before recording a pending activation, or preserve and enforce their origin through that pending activation while returning an attributed refusal. Preserve genuine operator pending-Return behavior. This leaves the original P1 incompletely fixed.

2. **P1: The palette unread-jump action explicitly erases a socket caller's context.** `Sources/ContentView.swift:6070-6071` invokes `operatorJumpToLatestUnread()` unconditionally. `Sources/AppDelegate.swift:11046-11047` then runs the jump inside `SocketCommandContext.withContext(nil)`. Concrete state/input: A is visible, C has the first eligible unread/attention target, and an agent submits the resolved “Jump to Latest Unread” palette command through `simulate_shortcut return`. The same socket-to-palette route reaches this action; `jumpToLatestUnread` → `openAttentionTarget` → `selectFeedTarget` selects C at `AppDelegate.swift:13655`, and `13671` raises its window. The setter sees nil, accepts the switch, and emits an operator `jump` cause instead of a blocked socket attempt. This requires no pending search. The direct jump shortcut already distinguishes `operatorIntent` at `11913`; the palette action does not. **Smallest fix:** retain socket context for socket-driven palette actions (call the ordinary gated jump for those requests), or refuse them at palette admission before invoking operator-only wrappers. Keep the real operator path's reentrant-context protection.

Both findings are source-path findings tied to scope 1 and the no-switch/no-activation acceptance requirement. Neither was reproduced in a guest during this delta review.

## Non-blocking

None. The previous P2 is repaired: nil cause parameters preserve the enclosing sidebar-folder cause, palette Next/Previous supply `palette`, and shortcut callers supply `shortcut`. The emitted-event test passes.

## Review and validation evidence

- Inspected the complete four-file delta and the connected palette/selection routes. Independently refreshed PR identity: it remains open at the exact reviewed head. The detached review checkout remained clean.
- Independent exact-head Atlas baseline, invocation `3e599978ab2d4c2293e05bf29bdec52e`, tag `review-323-r2`: **AgentWorkspaceSelectionTests 6/6, TerminalControllerSocketSecurityTests 6/6, EventLogTests 19/19; TEST SUCCEEDED**. The receipt identifies a clean source tree at the reviewed head.
- Independent required palette mutation, invocation `13caf75a2da7448999d7965159533659`: removed only the pre-hop refusal line in `focusPaletteSwitcherTarget` in a disposable checkout. Compilation succeeded; `testSocketPaletteSubmissionIsRefusedBeforeItsDeferredHop` failed with **two assertions**: `blockedTarget` was nil and the selected workspace changed. **TEST FAILED**, exit 65. Restored the mutation and retained its patch, logs and identity receipts locally. This proves coverage of the repaired helper, not the two earlier/action-specific routes above.
- Additional deferred-hop pass covered main-queue dispatch, Tasks and delayed-selector sites across the socket handlers and selection callers. The concrete additional lost-context hop is the pending palette search in finding 1. Main/deadline dispatch wrappers carry context; inspected async read/send/browser work does not select workspaces; deferred agent launch defaults to no selection; the cross-window reassertion route is behind a focus gate not admitted by socket moves. No other concrete socket-to-selection bypass was established in that pass.
- No builds/tests ran on Hyperion. No implementation-branch changes, commits, pushes, GitHub comments or merges. Owner validation `ev_01M3ZE4N0EGV5V20GETPG2ZPWT` and its baseline/mutation claims were checked against the independent runs above.

## Runtime proof still required

Add an Atlas regression at actual palette admission that holds a search pending, submits via the socket, releases the search and verifies A remains visible with no activation and an attributed refusal. Also exercise socket submission of the resolved unread-jump action with an eligible target in C. Verify genuine operator pending-submit and unread-jump still switch. Re-run the affected tests at the repaired head.

No guest was restarted for this review. Earlier guest evidence remains evidence for its earlier build, not exact-head proof.
